newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Hoechst first quarter below forecasts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Hoechst first quarter below forecasts.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Hoechst AG's first quarter results came in below forecasts but the company remained confident for the full year, predicting higher operating earnings on an adjusted basis.

"If economic conditions cooperate, we expect to post stronger results on a comparable basis," Hoechst chief financial officer Klaus-Juergen Schmieder told Reuters in a telephone interview, citing expected livelier demand, room to raise prices in some sectors, and favourable currency effects.

Full year sales at the world's largest chemicals group however are expected to be lower, seen between 42 and 47 billion marks ($27 billion) after last year's 51 billion marks. This reflects the sale of three units, including carbon and graphite maker group SGL Carbon AG, last year, Hoechst said.
While first quarter pre-tax profit slumped 33 percent to 831 million marks from a year ago, Hoechst said this actually represented a nine percent rise, on an adjusted basis.
Operating earnings dropped 22 percent to 1.03 billion marks but rose 20 percent on an adjusted basis, Hoechst said.
First quarter sales climbed one percent to 13.2 billion marks, with volume sales climbing two percent but prices easing two percent compared with the year earlier quarter.
Hoechst shares, hit by the softer than forecast results, ended bourse trade down two percent at 66.35 marks.

But analysts warned Hoechst's quarterly numbers are virtually meaningless at the moment as they were severely skewed while Hoechst underwent massive restructuring, streamlining its portfolio and turning itself into a strategic management holding company.
"The underlying trend however shows the company is roughly in line (with earlier-made forecasts)," said Andreas Schmidt, analyst at BZW in Frankfurt.

Analysts broadly welcomed Hoechst's more detailed quarterly earnings statement, saying the group appears to have upgraded its communications policies after being severely punished by investors for failing to adequately warn the market about an impending fourth quarter loss last year.
For example, Schmieder forecast the group would spend over 500 million marks on restructuring this year, outpacing the 400 million marks usually earmarked for annual restructuring costs.
Hoechst has already spent 195 million marks in restructuring costs during the first quarter, outpacing first quarter 1996 costs by 110 million marks.
Schmieder also said second quarter results would be significantly above first quarter results, especially as margins were expected to improve in several areas.
He declined to give details saying Hoechst was currently preparing more information for Tuesday's annual meeting.
Hoechst's prized pharmaceuticals division Hoechst Marion Roussel, posting a 15.5 percent rise in first quarter operating profit to 566 million marks, was faring well Schmieder said.
"We have the conquered the Seldane problem and our new allergy drug Allegra is doing very well."
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration had earlier this year said Seldane, a drug used to treat allergies, posed the risk of serious cardiac effects when not used properly.

Analysts said HMR's progress was welcome even though several noted that Hoechst's drugs pipeline remained rather weak and that joint-ventures in the drugs sector, although generally welcome, were initially raising costs.
Hoechst's agricultural business AgrEvo also fared very well in the first quarter, posting a 46 percent rise in operating profit to 176 million marks.
"Some of that is related to the weather," Schmieder said, noting that heavy rains improved sales of weedkillers.
($ = 1.726 German Marks)
